book.herbcraft.codex.title: Herbal Codex
book.herbcraft.entry.heard: You have heard of this, but never tried it yourself...
message.herbcraft.page.nothing_new: The page tells you nothing new.
book.herbcraft.codex.hint: Select an entry on the left.
nature.herbcraft.hint.generic: This thing has a nature yet to be read.
nature.herbcraft.hint.clearing: It seems to carry a cleansing nature.
nature.herbcraft.hint.toxic: Toxicity sleeps within. Taste with care.
nature.herbcraft.hint.sedating: Its breath is quieting and slow.
nature.herbcraft.hint.aquatic: Watery and cool on the tongue.
nature.herbcraft.hint.fiery: Fiery and rising, warm at once.
nature.herbcraft.hint.withered: A withered aura clings to it.
nature.herbcraft.hint.nether: A Nether nature, sharp and unruly.
nature.herbcraft.hint.floral: A floral scent lifts its medicine.
nature.herbcraft.hint.fungal: Fungal and subtle, hard to predict.
nature.herbcraft.hint.lunar: Dim and cool, carrying night air.
nature.herbcraft.hint.solar: Bright and warm with a touch of sun.
nature.herbcraft.hint.leafy: Leafy and astringent, clear on first bite.
nature.herbcraft.hint.slimy: Slick by nature and hard to forget.
nature.herbcraft.hint.addictive: Calming, but it may cling back.
nature.herbcraft.hint.curio: Strange in nature; one bite is not enough.
tooltip.herbcraft_cuisine.water_bowl.nat: Water tempers the herbs — suited for cuisine, not hodgepodge.
jade.herbcraft.title: Herbcraft
jade.herbcraft.unknown: Things have natures not yet known
advancements.herbcraft.root.title: Herbcraft
advancements.herbcraft.root.description: Step onto the path of edible herbs; every wild bite may now become knowledge.
advancements.herbcraft.open_codex.title: Open the Herbal Codex
advancements.herbcraft.open_codex.descri: Open the Herbal Codex: the left page is the index, the right page the record. Rumor is not proof; tasting makes it yours.
advancements.herbcraft.first_bite.title: First Taste
advancements.herbcraft.first_bite.descri: Taste a wild herb for the first time. Bind a Book with a Dandelion if you want to record what you learn.
advancements.herbcraft.eat_grass.title: Actually Eating Grass
advancements.herbcraft.eat_grass.descrip: Eat grass, fern, or another weed-like herb.
advancements.herbcraft.bitter_medicine.d: Eat a herb with harmful medicinal properties; bitterness is not always useless.
advancements.herbcraft.counter_poison.de: Experience a strange herb that clears or counters effects; poison and remedy may be one taste apart.
advancements.herbcraft.herb_stack_3.desc: Eating herbs in quick succession builds medicinal momentum; reward and risk both rise.
advancements.herbcraft.herb_stack_5.desc: The herb force gathers. Helpful effects may grow stronger, but backlash draws closer.
advancements.herbcraft.herb_stack_8.desc: The surge is high. One greedy bite may turn medicine into poison.
advancements.herbcraft.herb_overload.des: Overload your herb stack. Edible does not mean safe without measure.
advancements.herbcraft.first_page.title: Ink on a Torn Page
advancements.herbcraft.first_page.descri: A tattered page gives rumor; rumor is not truth until tasting proves it.
advancements.herbcraft.master_first_entr: Master your first Herbal Codex entry.
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.title: Herbal Codex Overview
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.line1: Edible does not mean harmless. A first taste gives only a rough impression.
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.line2: Pages bring rumors, not proof. Tasting and practice turn rumor into knowledge.
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.line3: Raw eating is risk; cuisine is preparation; alchemy is refinement. Each path has its use.
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.line4: Ordinary foods belong to the Ingredient Codex. Press [N] to view long-term nutrition.
message.herbcraft.herb_stack.stage_3: Bitterness curls on your tongue; the herbs begin to circle within.
message.herbcraft.herb_stack.stage_5: Potency rises; the plant nature seeps deeper.
message.herbcraft.herb_stack.stage_8: The medicine surges. Do not be greedy for another bite.
message.herbcraft.herb_stack.fade: The bitterness fades; the herb potency settles.
message.herbcraft.herb_stack.overload: Every medicine has poison. Herb potency overload!
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.harmonize: §bCold and heat harmonize; the medicine settles.
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.xiang_xu: §aMutual reinforcement: this positive effect is stronger.
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.xiang_shi: §aMutual assistance: this positive effect lasts longer.
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.xiang_sha: §bMutual detoxification: future toxic duration is reduced.
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.xiang_e: §eMutual antagonism: this medicine is weakened overall.
message.herbcraft.pharmacology.xiang_fan: §4Mutual incompatibility: this medicine fails and backfires!

book.herbcraft.guide.recognizing.title: Knowing Wild Herbs
book.herbcraft.guide.recognizing.line1: Seeing a plant gives shape; tasting it gives experience.
book.herbcraft.guide.recognizing.line2: A page may bring rumor, but rumor is only a lead.
book.herbcraft.guide.recognizing.tasted_: You have tasted %s herbs; the Codex is beginning to carry your own hand.
book.herbcraft.guide.recognizing.none: Begin with one common herb, taste lightly, and do not be greedy.
book.herbcraft.guide.knowledge_states.li: Unknown, Encountered, Heard, Tasted, and Mastered are the Codex's five steps of knowing.
Rumor gives leads, tasting proves sensation, and practice completes the record.
book.herbcraft.guide.knowledge_states.no: See it first, taste it next; the page clears as you act.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.title: Nature and Flavors
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.line1: Nature and flavor are not nutrition. They are herb-medicine rules: heat/cold describe tendency, while sweet, bitter, pungent, sour, salty, bland, and astringent describe flavor.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.line2: Heat and cold can build up or balance each other; flavors gently change effect chance, duration, strength, and side effects.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.none: Before tasting, nature and flavor can only be guessed from rumor and pages.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.first: You have tasted one herb and begun to sense warmth, cold, and flavor. Exact nature belongs in that herb's own entry.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.many: You have recognized %s flavor types. Similar flavor is a clue, not a guarantee.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven_emotions.line: Herb relations describe how herbs eaten close together interact. They are not a fixed recipe list.
Similar herbs may support each other; clashing herbs may weaken or backfire. Relations you trigger leave recent examples here.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven_emotions.tast: You have tasted %s herbs, enough to suspect that order can change medicine.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven_emotions.none: One herb cannot teach pairing. Taste a few more, then return.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.title: Medicinal Momentum
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.line1: Eating herbs in quick succession builds momentum; reward and risk rise together.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.stage3: You have felt the third turn: the herb force begins to gather.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.stage5: You have felt the fifth rise: helpful effects may grow stronger.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.stage8: You have felt the eighth surge: one greedy bite may backlash.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.overload: You have overloaded. Edible does not mean safe without measure.
book.herbcraft.guide.herb_stack.none: To test momentum, taste related herbs close together — but leave room to stop.
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.title: Ingredient Codex and Nutrition
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.line1: Ingredients are not herbs: no herb stack, no pharmacology, no pairing. But every meal nourishes.
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.tasted: You have tasted %s ingredients; their long-term nourishment is taking shape in the Ingredient Codex.
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.none: Eat ordinary foods first; only tasted ingredients reveal rough nutrition here.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.title: Pages and Errata
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.line1: Pages record rumor; errata tests truth. Mark doubtful claims before you trust them.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.heard: You have rumors recorded. Tasting, practice, or errata can make them reliable.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.verified: You have checked %s claims. The Codex remembers your judgment.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.none: Read a tattered page first, then return to judge its truth.
book.herbcraft.ingredients.overview.line: Ingredients are not herbs: they do not build herb stack or trigger pharmacology.
But every meal still nourishes. Grain, Flesh, Oil, Greens, and Fluids shape your long-term condition.
Only foods you have tasted reveal their rough nutrition here.
Press [N] to view your current nutrition state.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.tasted_once: You have tasted one herb and begun to sense warmth, cold, and flavor. Exact nature belongs in that herb's own entry.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.sweet: You have seen Sweet: sweet flavor tends to soften and often leans toward nourishment or recovery.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.bitter: You have seen Bitter: bitter flavor often clears, and may shave down gathered herb momentum.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.pungent: You have seen Pungent: pungent flavor moves medicine outward, but may trouble the stomach.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.sour: You have seen Sour: sour flavor gathers and holds; it can lengthen good sensations and shorten discomfort.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.astringent: You have seen Astringent: astringency draws inward, and in danger may help you hold on.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.salty: You have seen Salty: salty flavor often follows water and leans toward moistening movement.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.salty_water: You have seen Salty near water: close to water, its nature shows more clearly.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.bland: You have seen Bland: bland flavor does not contend, often dulling the edge of side effects.
book.herbcraft.guide.flavors.temperature: You have seen hot and cold balance each other: opposing nature can soften the edge.
You have seen heat build on heat: backlash draws closer.
You have seen cold gather on cold: medicine sinks and slows.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_xu: You have seen Mutual Need: %s and %s support each other, strengthening beneficial medicine.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_shi: You have seen Guiding Use: %s draws %s onward, carrying the medicine farther.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_sha: You have seen Mutual Killing: %s clears and suppresses the toxin of %s.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_wei: You have seen Mutual Fear: %s is restrained by %s, and its toxin withdraws.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_e: You have seen Mutual Aversion: %s and %s work against each other, weakening the whole dose.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.xiang_fan: You have seen Mutual Incompatibility: %s and %s clash in hot/cold toxicity, turning medicine back on you.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.count: You have seen this relation %s times; the latest example remains a useful reference.
guide.herbcraft.first_herb_bite: A wild taste lingers. Bind a Book with a Dandelion to make a Herbal Codex and record what you learn by tasting.
guide.herbcraft.first_codex_open: The left page is the index; the right page is the record. Rumors are not proof — tasting makes knowledge your own.
guide.herbcraft.first_page_read: A page gives rumor, not certainty. Mark doubts now; tasting or errata may prove them later.
guide.herbcraft.first_ingredient_tasted: Every meal nourishes. Ordinary foods do not carry herb nature, but the Ingredient Codex records their long-term nutrition. Press [N] to view your nutrition.
guide.herbcraft.first_correction: An uneven diet can be corrected. Eat what balances the excess, and the surplus will settle over time.
book.herbcraft.guide.seven.single: You have seen Single Action: %s acts mostly alone, with little tie to the herbs just eaten.
knowledge.herbcraft.food_nature.note: This is food first, yet its nature can still move flavor and qi.
knowledge.herbcraft.food_nature.codex_hi: Nutrition remains in the Ingredient Codex; this page records nature only.
book.herbcraft.entry.overview.line5: Press [T] to toggle day/night reading mode for different lighting.
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.line2: The Ingredient Codex records five nourishment dimensions: Grain, Flesh, Oil, Greens, and Fluids. These shape long-term condition, not herb pairing.
book.herbcraft.guide.ingredients.progres: You have tasted %s ingredients; their nourishment patterns can be read in the Ingredient Codex.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.line2: After marking a rumor, tasting or practice lets the page correct truth and falsehood over time.
book.herbcraft.guide.errata.progress: You have checked %s claims. The Codex remembers your judgment.
